data.title: Coordinated Posting Across an Account Cluster
data.summary:
A cluster of accounts published the same or near-identical content within a narrow time
window and across multiple platforms, in a pattern inconsistent with independent
behaviour.
data.description:
Synchronised posting is the most commonly cited coordination indicator and the one most
often overstated. Genuine communities also post the same thing at the same time, because
they read the same sources and respond to the same events. The indicator carries weight
only in combination: timing clustered more tightly than human behaviour explains, text
identical beyond what sharing would produce, and account histories that begin together.

Cross-posting adds strength. The same content appearing simultaneously on platforms with
different audiences is poorly explained by organic spread, since the usual route between
platforms is a person moving it deliberately.

State the inference and its limits. Coordination is observable; who is coordinating
usually is not, and the report should not let the first conclusion imply the second.
data.recommendation:
* Preserve the timing, text and account metadata that support the coordination assessment
  before the content is deleted.
* Report to platforms as coordinated inauthentic behaviour, with the cluster evidenced as
  a whole rather than account by account.
* Separate the assessment of coordination from any assessment of who is responsible.
data.short_recommendation: Evidence the cluster as a whole and report as coordinated behaviour.
